item.title: Why Texans stood pat while other AFC contenders made trades for impact players before deadline
item.description: Texans GM Nick Caserio did nothing at Tuesday's trade deadline after last month's deal for Marvin Harrison Jr., trusting recent progress and a healthier roster to fuel Houston's playoff push. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) The NFL's trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon without the Houston Texans making any additional moves. While contending teams like the Jaguars , Bills , Chiefs and Broncos all made trades for players they hope will make an impact, the Texans were content with what they had done last month when they traded a second-round pick for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . That, in a sense, should be viewed as their trade deadline move. The difference between those teams and the Texans is that the Jaguars, Bills, Chiefs and Broncos all have a 6-2 record or better, while Houston is 3-5 and has serious ground to make up. The Texans also currently have a 32% chance of making the playoffs , according to the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. Trading another asset for a player they'd hope would make an impact this season would have been a huge gamble. The Texans did check in on running backs across the league, one league source said, but ultimately decided not to make a move. They also ended up keeping the five offensive tackles on their 53-man roster. That the Texans didn't make any more significant trades at the deadline indicates that they are both satisfied with the makeup of this team and the progress they've made over the past few games, though more is needed. The offense is coming off its best game of the season against the Chargers . And the defense, which was playing the worst offense in the NFL, made strides in that game . The Texans are also getting healthy at the right time. Nickel corner Jalen Pitre made his return after missing the previous two games with a shoulder injury, while running back David Montgomery, who is dealing with a groin injury, is expected to return within the next two weeks, if not Sunday, in what Houston hopes will be a boost to its running game . item.title: Texas high school football team challenges TAPPS playoff ruling in court
item.description: Argyle Liberty Christian's court hearing was scheduled for Tuesday as the Texas high school football powerhouse seeks to overturn a TAPPS ruling that removed it from the playoffs. (Steve Hamm/Dallas Morning News) Argyle Liberty Christian is taking its fight for a spot in the Texas high school football playoffs to court. A hearing on the school's requests for a temporary restraining order and injunction is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 10. Liberty Christian is seeking to overturn a TAPPS ruling that removed its football team from the Division I playoffs, according to The Dallas Morning News. Liberty Christian sued TAPPS after the organization's executive board ruled that the school used an ineligible player, wide receiver Jace Johnson, in violation of its "follow the coach" rule. The ruling required the school to forfeit games in which Johnson played, eliminating the team from postseason contention. The dispute centers on whether Liberty Christian assistant coach Antonio Griffin previously coached Johnson on a 7-on-7 football team. ALSO READ: Johnson finishes No. 1 in the Express-News football power rankings TAPPS officials said the school's athletic department and coaching staff "knew or should have known" about Johnson's connection to Griffin's Lionhearted 7-on-7 program before the season began. Liberty Christian and fellow plaintiff Jericho McCants are challenging the ruling, alleging that emails submitted as evidence were altered and that Griffin never coached Johnson. The Dallas Morning News reported that parents allege an email was changed to describe Griffin's involvement with the program as "Owned and Coached by Coach Griff," rather than the original wording, "Owned by Coach Griff." Undra Hendrix II, a Lionhearted coach, told the newspaper he coaches Johnson's 18U 7-on-7 team, while Griffin owns the program. The hearing will address whether Liberty Christian can temporarily block TAPPS' ruling as it continues its effort to return to the playoffs. item.title: Brandon Aiyuk's agent weighs in on 49ers acrimony, the $13M dispute, and WR's future
item.description: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, speaking to reporters before the 2024 season, appeared at 49ers headquarters last week for the first time since December. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Drew Rosenhaus didn't speak with Kyle Shanahan when the NFL agent met with San Francisco 49ers officials on Friday, but he clearly read what the head coach said regarding Rosenhaus' new client, Brandon Aiyuk , earlier that day. "Judging from the comments from Coach Shanahan," Rosenhaus said, "it doesn't sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back." That unintended humor was part of Rosenhaus' appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Tuesday, when Rosenhaus discussed the future of the in-limbo Aiyuk, who was reinstated to the NFL on Monday after passing a physical. The 49ers were granted a two-game roster exemption that expires on Nov. 23, giving them time to negotiate a divorce before Aiyuk would occupy a spot on their 53-man roster. As Rosenhaus has surmised, the 49ers aren't keeping Aiyuk, 28, who has taken a blowtorch to their relationship by ghosting the team last season - prompting his placement on the reserve/left the squad list - before taking shots at Shanahan and general manager John Lynch in a string of social-media posts that began last summer. Said Shanahan when asked for his thoughts before Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with team officials Friday: "I could (not) care less." A potential holdup to Aiyuk's inevitable release: The 49ers believe Aiyuk owes them about $13 million in bonus money. That financial issue is why the NFL Management Council and NLPA were involved in Friday's meeting, and arbitration could reportedly be used to settle the matter. Rosenhaus suggested he and Aiyuk were trying to get the 49ers to agree to a lesser amount. "As far as the money that's allegedly owed - the $13 million, whatever it is - he hasn't paid anything yet," he said. "That's something that we'll work out separate and distinct from the issue of him playing. Hopefully we'll work something out to the benefit of Brandon's, and something that's fair. And that's also part of my job." Rosenhaus said he's representing Aiyuk because he wanted to "help" him. Aiyuk's behavior since leaving the 49ers last season has prompted questions about whether NFL teams would be wary about signing him when his conduct is coupled with his medical file. Aiyuk hasn't played since October 2024 due to a knee injury that included a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus damage. "I think he's in a really good place," Rosenhaus said. "He met with the 49ers. He did a good job in the meeting with them. He said hello to John Lynch. He met with the team. I just feel like he's in a good place. And getting to know him over the last week, I'm confident in his future moving forward." As far as Aiyuk's playing future, Rosenhaus said he was "100%" healthy and prepared to work out for other teams once his split from the 49ers is finalized. item.title: New 49ers receiver Keenan Allen once beefed with Mike Evans on social media
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans speaks during a news conference following a win over the Seattle Seahawks in an NFL football game in Seattle, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. (Lindsey Wasson/AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson) The San Francisco 49ers not only bolstered their receiving corps when they traded for Keenan Allen ahead of the trade deadline on Tuesday, they also reunited two former feuding players who got into it online. Back in 2020, a little less than four months after the NFL decided to move forward with a regularly scheduled season during the COVID-19 pandemic, Allen, then with the Chargers, took issue with the annual NFL Top 100 list of the league's best players. Specifically, he was incensed that he was placed at No. 77, so much so that he tweeted about it and tagged other players he thought he was better than: Tyreek Hill, Mike Evans and Chris Godwin. "Ok I'm tired of biten my tongue…@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin… (and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better reciever than me! Faster than me…every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!" Allen wrote . It's not hard to see where Allen's frustrations were coming from as he was ranked No. 38 on the list the year before. He might have been so upset that he forgot to check that he tagged the correct Chris Godwin in his post (he did not). Regardless, Evans replied to the callout. "You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em," Evans replied . "I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro." You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em. I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro - Mike Evans (@MikeEvans13_) July 27, 2020 Allen did not respond, but did follow up his own post with , "IM THE BEST WR IN THE AFC WEST!!! Without question!!!" Statistically speaking, Evans came out on top at the end of that season. He finished with 1,006 yards and 13 touchdowns on 70 receptions as his Tom Brady-led Buccaneers team won the Super Bowl. Allen still had an incredible year, grabbing 100 receptions in 14 games for 992 yards and eight touchdowns. Six years is a long time for people to think about some Twitter beef that lasted all of two posts - and one side even conceding some respect for the other. Still, if both players could tap into the competitiveness that led to the kinds of seasons they respectively put together that year, then the Niners are in for one hell of a receiving duo. item.title: Tiger Woods drops strongest hint yet that golf comeback could happen soon
item.description: Tiger Woods says he's feeling better and hinted he could return to professional golf as soon as the Hero World Challenge in December. Woods was asked about his comeback plans during a public appearance on Tuesday, Nov. 10, and the 15-time major winner gave a positive update going into the limited-field event he hosts annually in the Bahamas in less than a month. Woods, 50, has been away from competition since The Open Championship in July 2024 due to a variety of injuries and personal setbacks. His comeback attempt ahead of last year's Masters was derailed by a DUI arrest and rehab stint stemming from a car crash in March that led to a plea deal and the suspension of his driver's license . "I'm feeling better. No doubt about that. I've been training quite a bit. I will be at the Hero," Woods said through laughter in brief comments to SiriusXM's PGA Tour Radio . "I'm there either way, so I'll see you there." The video posted to social media did not show any other questions asked of Woods, who could either be a player-host at the tournament or simply serve as host for the event. RELATED: Tiger Woods on hand as son makes Florida State decision official When could Tiger Woods return to golf? This year's Hero World Challenge is set for Dec. 3-6, and tournament organizers left three spots in the 20-golfer field open for exemptions. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick and Justin Thomas are among the notable golfers who have already committed to play . There have been signs in recent weeks that Woods is gearing up for a return to the course. Tiger Woods says he's "feeling better" and has been training quite a bit. item.title: Magic Johnson pinpoints why LA Lakers are really better without LeBron James this season
item.description: Photo by Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers legend Magic Johnson has offered his thoughts on the team’s impressive 10-2 record. After beating the Atlanta Hawks, the LA Lakers moved to the top of the Western Conference. They became the first team in the NBA this season to reach 10 wins. After the win, Skip Bayless posted on X, referring to LeBron James, “The Los Angeles Lakers now have the NBA’s best record. No, they do not miss him.” Magic Johnson has now had his say on the Lakers’ improvement, and he believes the team is simply faster and mentally tougher. He posted: “Last year, the Lakers were a slow team that got beat in transition – but not this season. This team is mentally and physically tougher, and that’s why they’re 10-2!” After losing LeBron James in the offseason, the Lakers were able to use his salary to focus on other areas of the team. They have added more depth and their bench appears stronger than it did last season, with Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton among the additions making an impact. Johnson praises JJ Redick Magic Johnson believes LA Lakers head coach JJ Redick deserves the credit for the improvement, despite Luka Doncic’s incredible performances, averaging 39.3 ppg. Johnson says he has seen signs of development from Redick and is pleased with his impact, now in his third season as a head coach. He posted: “The Lakers’ win over the Hawks yesterday showed that JJ Redick has become a great NBA coach. “His in-game switch from man-to-man to a zone defense changed the trajectory of the game, and he’s outstanding at drawing up plays out of timeouts!” The Lakers are next in action against the Milwaukee Bucks. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Fox Sports announcer steps down from NASCAR booth
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The NASCAR Truck Series will have a new television play-by-play voice in 2027. On Tuesday, Jamie Little announced on social media that, starting next season, she will focus on NASCAR Cup Series pit reporting and select IndyCar races. “Starting next season, my focus will be on the NASCAR Cup Series pit road and select IndyCar races,” Little wrote. She also cited her family as a factor in the decision, adding, “My kids are still young and deserve more of my time.” CHANGING THINGS UP A BIT IN 2027! https://t.co/xTyW26gAnY — Jamie Little (@JamieLittleTV) November 10, 2026 Little had served as Fox Sports’ NASCAR Truck Series and ARCA Menards Series play-by-play announcer since 2021, becoming the first woman to serve as the lead television play-by-play announcer for a national motorsports series. She became the full-time Truck Series announcer in 2023, while continuing her pit-reporting duties for NASCAR Cup Series broadcasts on Fox Sports. Little is perhaps best known for her highly praised pit reporting, a role she has held with Fox Sports since 2015. She previously worked on ESPN’s NASCAR and IndyCar coverage before also joining Fox’s IndyCar broadcasts in 2025. Her broadcasting career also includes reporting for the X Games, dating back to 1998. Throughout her career, Little has covered numerous Daytona 500s and Indianapolis 500s. Her 2027 move will allow her to refocus on pit reporting for NASCAR Cup Series races and select IndyCar events. Notably, Little called Kyle Busch’s final career NASCAR victory at Dover Motor Speedway, less than a week before his death. An absolutely DOMINATING NASCAR Truck Series win for Kyle Busch at Dover! https://t.co/2g5wQVVcnI — FOX: NASCAR (@NASCARONFOX) May 15, 2026 During the 2026 Truck Series and ARCA seasons, Little split time in the booth, sharing play-by-play duties with rising broadcaster Eric Brennan, best known for his work on the CARS Tour, and Brent Stover, longtime CBS Sports host and play-by-play announcer. Both Brennan and Stover received considerable praise from fans for their commentary throughout the season. However, Fox Sports has yet to announce who will take over Little’s role in the Truck Series booth in 2027. The NASCAR Truck Series will have 25 races during the 2027 season, all airing exclusively across Fox Sports networks. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. item.title: What’s the plan for Utah’s goaltending situation?
item.description: Utah Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa (33) watches as a puck slips past him during an NHL game against the Pittsburgh Penguins at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News Is there another position in sports as fickle as goaltending? One minute, you’re the solution to the problem. The next, you are the problem. One day, fans are chanting your name, and the next, they’re essentially calling for your head on a platter. Heck, it might be the most hot-and-cold job in the world. Karel Vejmelka has experienced both sides of the coin in the two-and-a-bit seasons he’s played for the Utah Mammoth. He saved the season in Year 1 when Connor Ingram stepped away from hockey for family and health reasons. In Year 2, he was the only goalie the team could consistently rely on. In both seasons, he earned “Veggie” chants on a near-nightly basis at the Delta Center, and his biggest fans started wearing broccoli hats to support him. Now, a little more than a month into Year 3, many of those same fans hope to see him traded. Vejmelka tries to stay positive. “I think so, yeah,” he said in response to the Deseret News’ question of whether he’s playing up to his standard. “I think, of course, I can be even better, but I just do my best every single day to get better every day. “So just need to keep working on it and just, you know, be positive and just keep playing and just be a key player on the ice. Just give us a chance to play and to win the game every single time.” League-wide, save percentages have been down the last few years. More goals equates to more fan excitement so that’s how the league wants it to be, but Vejmelka is on pace to record the lowest save percentage of his career by a wide margin, and he currently has the second-worst goals saved above expected in the NHL, according to MoneyPuck . Even so, the Mammoth are finding ways to win games. “We’re just kind of in the same spot where we (were) last year,” Vejmelka said. “So we have enough points to be in the in the (top) half in the standings, but we just need to keep going and just be even better.” Sebastian Cossa, the rookie goalie whom Utah acquired this summer in one of the biggest trades of the franchise’s brief history, has similar numbers to Vejmelka and a similar outlook on them. “We’re getting most of the results, which has been good. item.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick (the Vikings’ second in the round) Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who general manager John Spytek confirmed Tuesday afternoon will be the starter moving forward. Here are some notes about their deadline decisions: The Raiders, at 4-5, didn’t decide to make it a fire sale. They also didn’t opt to add at the trade deadline either as they have lost five of the last six games after starting 3-0. NFL reporter Jordan Schulz reported that the Raiders did receive recent trade calls on star defensive end Maxx Crosby, but resisted them after a nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens in March. Because the Raiders have already agreed to trade Crosby once, expect them to receive more calls in the future, including next offseason. There is no word if the Raiders had any interest in pending free agents, wide receiver Tre Tucker and safety Jeremy Chinn. It will be interesting to see if they try to extend them in the offseason. Spytek said he received calls on multiple players without getting into detail. Despite needs at some posts, including at wide receiver and defensive tackle, the Raiders did not add at the deadline. Spytek said the Cousins’ trade is not an indication the team is giving up on the season. Coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza is prepared, physically and mentally, for this task and he praised Cousin for his influence on the rookie. Spytek said Mendoza has passed every test since being drafted and he helped the Raiders make the tough decision to deal Cousins. Spytek said Mendoza’s play in practice was difficult to ignore. Spytek said he only received calls on Cousins and did not make any himself. The talks with Minnesota emerged Tuesday morning after Carson Wentz’s horrible showing in a loss Monday night. Spytek said the team did not expect this to happen before Tuesday, thus he had no previous conversations with Cousins about it.
